00011| Welcome to the Next.js documentation!
00012| 
00013| ## What is Next.js?
00014| 
00015| Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. You use React Components to build user interfaces, and Next.js for additional features and optimizations.
00016| 
00017| It also automatically configures lower-level tools like bundlers and compilers. You can instead focus on building your product and shipping quickly.
00018| 
00019| Whether you're an individual developer or part of a larger team, Next.js can help you build interactive, dynamic, and fast React applications.
00020| 
00021| ## How to use the docs
00022| 
00023| The docs are organized into 3 sections:
00024| 
00025| - [Getting Started](/docs/app/getting-started): Step-by-step tutorials to help you create a new application and learn the core Next.js features.
00026| - [Guides](/docs/app/guides): Tutorials on specific use cases, choose what's relevant to you.
00027| - [API Reference](/docs/app/api-reference): Detailed technical reference for every feature.
00028| 
00029| Use the sidebar to navigate through the sections, or search (`Ctrl+K` or `Cmd+K`) to quickly find a page.
00030| 
00031| ## App Router and Pages Router
00032| 
00033| Next.js has two different routers:
00034| 
00035| - **App Router**: The newer router that supports new React features like Server Components.
00036| - **Pages Router**: The original router, still supported and being improved.
00037| 
00038| At the top of the sidebar, you'll notice a dropdown menu that allows you to switch between the [App Router](/docs/app) and the [Pages Router](/docs/pages) docs.
00039| 
00040| ### React version handling
00041| 
00042| The App Router and Pages Router handle React versions differently:
00043| 
00044| - **App Router**: Uses [React canary releases](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries) built-in, which include all the stable React 19 changes, as well as newer features being validated in frameworks, prior to a new React release.
00045| 
00046| - **Pages Router**: Uses the React version installed in your project's `package.json`.
00047| 
00048| This approach ensures new React features work reliably in the App Router while maintaining backwards compatibility for existing Pages Router applications.
00049| 
00050| ## Pre-requisite knowledge
00051| 
00052| Our documentation assumes some familiarity with web development. Before getting started, it'll help if you're comfortable with:
00053| 
00054| - HTML
00055| - CSS
00056| - JavaScript
00057| - React
00058| 
00059| If you're new to React or need a refresher, we recommend starting with our [React Foundations course](/learn/react-foundations), and the [Next.js Foundations course](/learn/dashboard-app) that has you building an application as you learn.
00060| 
00061| ## Accessibility
00062| 
00063| For the best experience when using a screen reader, we recommend using Firefox and NVDA, or Safari and VoiceOver.
00064|

Welcome to the Next.js documentation!

## What is Next.js?

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. You use React Components to build user interfaces, and Next.js for additional features and optimizations.

It also automatically configures lower-level tools like bundlers and compilers. You can instead focus on building your product and shipping quickly.

Whether you're an individual developer or part of a larger team, Next.js can help you build interactive, dynamic, and fast React applications.

00019| The Metadata APIs can be used to define your application metadata for improved SEO and web shareability and include:
00020| 
00021| 1. [The static `metadata` object](#static-metadata)
00022| 2. [The dynamic `generateMetadata` function](#generated-metadata)
00023| 3. Special [file conventions](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata) that can be used to add static or dynamically generated [favicons](#favicons) and [OG images](#static-open-graph-images).
00024| 
00025| With all the options above, Next.js will automatically generate the relevant `<head>` tags for your page, which can be inspected in the browser's developer tools.
00026| 
00027| The `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function exports are only supported in Server Components.
00028| 
00029| ## Default fields
00030| 
00031| There are two default `meta` tags that are always added even if a route doesn't define metadata:
00032| 
00033| - The [meta charset tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta#attr-charset) sets the character encoding for the website.
00034| - The [meta viewport tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Viewport_meta_tag) sets the viewport width and scale for the website to adjust for different devices.
00035| 
00036| ```html
00037| <meta charset="utf-8" />
00038| <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
00039| ```
00040| 
00041| The other metadata fields can be defined with the `Metadata` object (for [static metadata](#static-metadata)) or the `generateMetadata` function (for [generated metadata](#generated-metadata)).
00042| 
00043| ## Static metadata
00044| 
00045| To define static metadata, export a [`Metadata` object](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#metadata-object) from a static [`layout.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) or [`page.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) file. For example, to add a title and description to the blog route:
00046| 
00047| ```tsx filename="app/blog/layout.tsx" switcher
00048| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
00049| 
00050| export const metadata: Metadata = {
00051|   title: 'My Blog',
00052|   description: '...',
00053| }
00054| 
00055| export default function Layout() {}
00056| ```
00057| 
00058| ```jsx filename="app/blog/layout.js" switcher
00059| export const metadata = {
00060|   title: 'My Blog',
00061|   description: '...',
00062| }
00063| 
00064| export default function Layout() {}
00065| ```
00066| 
00067| You can view a full list of available options, in the [`generateMetadata` documentation](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#metadata-fields).
00068| 
00069| ## Generated metadata
00070| 
00071| You can use [`generateMetadata`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata) function to `fetch` metadata that depends on data. For example, to fetch the title and description for a specific blog post:
00072| 
00073| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00074| import type { Metadata, ResolvingMetadata } from 'next'
00075| 
00076| type Props = {
00077|   params: Promise<{ slug: string }>
00078|   searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>
00079| }
00080| 
00081| export async function generateMetadata(
00082|   { params, searchParams }: Props,
00083|   parent: ResolvingMetadata
00084| ): Promise<Metadata> {
00085|   const slug = (await params).slug
00086| 
00087|   // fetch post information
00088|   const post = await fetch(`https://api.vercel.app/blog/${slug}`).then((res) =>
00089|     res.json()
00090|   )
00091| 
00092|   return {
00093|     title: post.title,
00094|     description: post.description,
00095|   }
00096| }
00097| 
00098| export default function Page({ params, searchParams }: Props) {}
00099| ```

00006| The `layout` file is used to define a layout in your Next.js application.

00049| }

These will primarily be the component of a child [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (if it exists) or [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), but could also be other special files like [Loading](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) or [Error](/docs/app/getting-started/error-handling) when applicable.
